open_decisions.text: rquickjs 0.14.0 (bundled QuickJS-NG 0.16.2 C, conditional native candidate) vs boa_engine 0.22.0 (pure Rust, no -sys, ~43 normal deps). Boa RuntimeLimits has loop/recursion/stack/backtrace limits but NO heap limit, so a heap bomb cannot be denied in-process: Boa needs the separate worker-process design (RSS/CPU/wall deadline enforced by the parent, same isolation pattern as score-plugin) before it can claim EXPR-PROVIDER quotas. rquickjs has set_memory_limit/set_max_stack_size plus a cooperative interrupt handler but is C/FFI (rquickjs-sys name rejected by the probe pure_registry_name; needs steward scoped exemption + approved entry; feature graph must pin default features only, never full/loader/dyn-load/futures/chrono/allocator). Neither chosen; no dependency requested yet (builders/dep-requests.jsonl untouched). Needed from steward/lead: (1) probe policy for rquickjs-sys, (2) decision whether the worker-process slice is mandatory for any backend, (3) approval path for boa_parser/boa_ast (validator) pins.

Brief step 1 (AST allowlist validator with boa_parser, source_sha256, span table) NOT started: needs boa_parser/boa_ast dep requests; provider accepts any source and relies on the adapter. A token scan was deliberately not added (denying eval/Function names alone is not a control, STU-MOT-258).

decisions.text: ScriptedEngine interprets fixed command words only; it must never grow into a JS evaluator (adoption review rejects an own interpreter). It exists so provider policy is provable without a native engine.
MOT-259 has no runtime-error code. Thrown reference error -> ReferenceMissing, any other thrown error -> Unsupported. UNVERIFIED mapping; revisit when the spec adds a runtime-error outcome.
motion-js-es2018@1 is a working identifier, not taken from the spec.

Wall-clock deadline is a cooperative resource guard (machine-speed dependent, EXPR-PROVIDER-04); the deterministic budget is Fuel. Both surface as Budget; the kind is only visible in ProviderStats denial counters.
A Budget error returned by HostRead (fuel exhausted inside a host read) is mapped to BudgetKind::Fuel and cannot be caught by script code.
